workingTitle: Twelve dust grains reveal ancient water beyond Neptune
publicationStatus: Peer-reviewed Science Advances article published online 11 November 2026
coreFacts: The study analyzed 12 hydrated interplanetary dust particles collected from Earth's stratosphere by NASA high-altitude aircraft.
Solar energetic particle track densities of about 10^10 to 10^11 per square centimeter support an origin beyond the giant planets, most plausibly the Kuiper Belt.
Electron microscopy found water-altered clay minerals, while UCLA ion microprobe measurements established the particles' oxygen-isotope compositions.
Mass-balance modeling inferred ancient water strongly depleted in oxygen-16, with estimated delta-18O and delta-17O near +157 and +153 per mil.
The rarity of this signature in inner-system meteorites suggests limited mixing; Saturn and perhaps the ice giants may have acted as a barrier.

sources.label: A primordial heavy water reservoir in the outer solar system

sourceStatus: Peer-reviewed Science Advances paper verified through PubMed and the full NASA-hosted author manuscript; NASA and UCLA releases corroborate the interpretation.
caveats: The particles' distant origin is inferred from solar energetic particle track density rather than traced to a named Kuiper Belt body.
The ancient water composition is reconstructed by mass balance from hydrated minerals, not measured from surviving liquid or ice.
The idea that Saturn and the ice giants restricted inward transport is an interpretation supported by isotopic contrast and disk simulations.
